target_customer: Energy intensive businesses with many properties and utility bills
problem: Companies lack one place for utility data, so they miss billing errors and savings. Leafpress centralized utility data with OCR and AI.
business_model: B2B SaaS for energy data management
product_category: AI energy management and utility data

founders.name: Devi Jha
education: Harvard, Computer Science (YC page says left without a degree; launch post says alum)
founders.background_notes: Launch post lists energy teams at P&G and Spotify.

technical_complexity.rationale: Parsing heterogeneous utility bills and integrating utility portals required OCR and many custom integrations, which a two person team could start but not finish quickly.

defensibility.rationale: Utility integrations could lock in customers, but no proprietary data or contracts are documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response was found; the founders themselves moved to a document intelligence product.

market_need_then: The launch post says energy intensive businesses struggle to manage energy use, pay bills on time and plan retrofits, and calls existing solutions fragmented and manual.

branding.domain_note: Dataset lists trycardinal.ai, which redirects to trycardinal.com.

rebrands.why: the founders moved from energy data to document intelligence and later an outbound revenue platform; the YC launch post uses both names

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found; the name was dropped for Cardinal.

pivots.from: AI energy and utility data management (Leafpress)
pivots.to: Cardinal, a document intelligence API built after the founders struggled to extract data from utility bills
pivots.why: per a runtimewire article; the date is not given

pivots.to: Cardinal AI revenue platform for outbound sales
pivots.why: per a runtimewire article published 2026-07-30; customers named include Deepgram, Giga and Mintlify

outcome_analysis: Leafpress did not die as a team: its founders turned the utility bill problem into Cardinal, first a document intelligence API and then an outbound revenue platform in 2026, and Cardinal went through YC again. The YC page for Leafpress says the energy software company was sold to Johnson Controls, but no independent source confirms that. The reason Leafpress is inactive is therefore a pivot, not a documented failure.
notes: The Johnson Controls sale appears only in the YC founder bios (possibly a different company) and two Johnson Controls searches found no Leafpress deal, so it is unverified and exit stays unknown. The pre-seed rests on one aggregator (VCBacked). The trycardinal.ai site redirects to trycardinal.com and the page was not read after redirect. The YC page lists a founding date of 2025, likely for Cardinal. No competitor sources dated near mid 2023 were found, so that list is empty.
